epoch._epoch_length: epoch k lasts 2,100·(k+1) Bitcoin blocks: 2,100, 4,200, 6,300 … ; epoch k is seeded by Bitcoin height H0 + 2,100·k(k+1)/2
epoch._claims: open 24 h after the root; close two weeks later or when the next epoch opens, whichever first

eligibility._exclude_todo: Placeholder — real exclusions (founder/operator, token, vesting, pool; lowercase) are supplied at genesis, not committed to this public file. v2 uses snapshot_v2.py --exclude; they are bound into the committed header.
_doc: E_k = addresses a satisfying ALL of (whitepaper §4.1):
(1) a sent >= 1 transaction in Base blocks (B-W, B]   — the enumeration (sender scan); checked as nonce(a,B) > nonce(a,B-W)
(2) a is a regular wallet at B: no code, or an EIP-7702 delegation

(3) balance(a, B) >= min AND balance(a, B-W) >= min   — min = $100 of ETH at the snapshot's public rate (header min=<wei>, ethusd=<cents>): about a thousandth of a bitcoin, held through the whole epoch, not borrowed for a day
epoch 0 only: balance_Base(a, B) + balance_L1(a, L) < max0   — max0 = $100,000 of ETH at genesis (header max0=<wei>); first draw for those holding less than about one bitcoin's worth
(4) nonce(a, B) >= base_min_nonce OR nonce_L1(a, L) >= l1_min_nonce ; and nonce(a, B) <= base_max_nonce   — has used the chain; is not infrastructure
(5) j >= 1 only: a was not drawn in any epoch i <= j-1   — one wallet, one payout; checked against the published winners files alone (no claim state, so no eth_call)
minus the exclusion list. B, W, L, exclusions (and H0, max0 for epoch 0) are in the snapshot header, which is hashed and committed.
Epoch 0: B = the deployment (genesis) block of the token — not chosen by the operator.
eligibility._exclude_note: Filled BEFORE the genesis snapshot with: token contract, vesting contract, pool, founder, operator (lowercase). Bound into every committed snapshot header (exclude=...). Never changed afterwards.
eligibility._exclude_past_recipients: ONE WALLET, ONE PAYOUT. From the second draw on (j >= 1): an address drawn in ANY earlier epoch (i <= j-1) is excluded from every later draw, whether or not it claimed. A wallet is therefore paid at most once and can receive at most MAX_PIECE (50) coins in the whole run. Verifiable from the published winners files alone — no claim state is read, so no eth_call and no waiting for a window to close. NOTE: this is a rule of the draw, enforced when the list is built and checkable by re-deriving it; the contract itself only caps a single claim at 50 coins and only prevents claiming twice within one epoch.
eligibility._min_usd: floor: $100 of ETH (about a thousandth of a bitcoin) held both at B and at B-W; converted to wei at each snapshot from the public ETH-USD spot (Coinbase) and written into the header as min=<wei> together with the rate (ethusd=<cents>)
eligibility._genesis_cap_usd: genesis only: Base balance at B + Ethereum balance at L below $100,000 of ETH (about one bitcoin), converted at the genesis snapshot and written as max0=<wei>
eligibility._min_wei: FALLBACK ONLY. ops/epoch.py always passes --min-wei computed from the live Coinbase spot at snapshot time, and verify.py asserts min×ethusd ≈ $100 from the header — this baked value is used only if snapshot.py is run standalone without --min-wei.

snapshot_format: line 1: '# 2BTC snapshot epoch=K block=B window=W l1block=L min=WEI ethusd=CENTS [h0=H max0=WEI] rule=v4 exclude=<comma-separated or none>'; then one lowercase 0x-address per line, sorted ascending (bytewise), LF newlines; commit = sha256(file bytes)

process._doc: Operational rules a verifier checks (whitepaper §4.2). The operator's discretion is WHEN to snapshot (k >= 1), never the seed.
process.genesis_snapshot_block: genesisBlock() of the contract (deployment block) — fixed, not chosen
process._snapshot_max_age: for k >= 1, timestamp(B) and timestamp(L) must be within 12 h before the commit transaction
process._commit_lead: commit must land while Bitcoin tip <= H_k - 36 (≈ 6 h expected); the tooling refuses otherwise
process._verifier_tiers: timestamp(H_k) - commitTime: >= 4 h OK; 2–4 h LATE (warning); < 2 h TAINTED (indistinguishable from a commit made after the block; Bitcoin timestamps are miner-set within ~2 h); <= 0 INVALID
process._genesis_h0: for epoch 0 the operator sets H0 = (Bitcoin tip at COMMIT time) + 36, writes it into the header, hashes, and calls commitSnapshot(0, hash, H0); the contract fixes H0 forever (one-shot commit)
process._seed_confirmations: open an epoch only once H_k has >= 6 confirmations; cross-check the hash with two independent sources; the Bitcoin chain is authoritative
process._claim_delay: claims open 24 h after a root is posted — time for anyone to recompute the draw
process.unclaimed: when the next epoch opens, the previous epoch's unclaimed coins are halved: half burned, half added to the new epoch's cap
process.skip: a tainted or impossible epoch may be skipped on-chain (skipEpoch), only after the genesis commit: it is a public re-roll — half of that epoch's coins are burned, half move to the next epoch; skipped epochs do not advance the founder's vesting
process.genesis_l1_block: for epoch 0, L = the highest Ethereum block whose timestamp <= timestamp(B) (deterministic; not chosen)
process._epoch_schedule: H_k = H0 + 2,100·k(k+1)/2; the on-chain guard requires 4/5 of epoch k-1's nominal length between openings
